newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's M1 money supply up 1.8 percent in June.
newsitem.headline: Israel's M1 money supply up 1.8 percent in June.

text.p: Israel's M1 money supply rose a preliminary 1.8 percent in June to 18.29 billion shekels, the Bank of Israel said on Thursday.
The rise followed an 0.4 percent decline in May and a 1.8 percent rise in April. In June 1996, M1 fell 0.2 percent.
The June figure brought the M1 increase the 12 months to June 30 to 14.5 percent, compared with 11.9 percent in calendar 1996 and 16.5 percent in calendar 1995, the central bank said.
The relatively sharp rise in M1 follows the release of an unexpectedly high June consumer price index (CPI) on Tuesday. The CPI rose 1.1 percent on the back on a sharp increase in housing prices.

The CPI and money supply figures are two parameters the central bank uses in determining interest rates. The bank is scheduled to announce its August monetary programme, including interest rates, July 28.
The Bank of Israel said total credit rose 1.1 percent in June to 285 billion shekels slowing from rises of 1.4 percent in May and 2.1 percent in April.
In the 12 months to June 30, credit rose 17.5 percent, versus 20 percent in calendar 1996 and 23.4 percent in calendar 1995.

The growth in unlinked shekel credit dropped sharply to 0.2 percent in June to 86.3 billion shekels. It rose 1.3 percent in May and 1.6 percent in April. Unlinked credit grew 8.8 percent in the last 12 months, slowing from 13.4 percent in calendar 1996.
